scope: Fresh source and evidence review of EXT-D-0150 origin-tab repair, dispatcher invariants, docs, and guard design. No tests, build, browser, release, database, or deployment actions were performed by this reviewer.

prior_finding_disposition.finding: Page-registered WebMCP calls lose sender.tab.id and can retarget the focused tab; missing or closed origins need honest refusal; procedure text must match current document.modelContext and external confirmation behavior.
prior_finding_disposition.status: ADDRESSED IN SOURCE AND PROCEDURES; NATIVE ACCEPTANCE STILL PENDING
evidence: src/lib/background/bootstrap.ts now rejects missing sender.tab.id and a tab that chrome.tabs.get cannot resolve, then passes assignedTabId to dispatch.
src/lib/tools/dispatch.ts preserves assignedTabId in ToolContext and rechecks page-origin availability before dispatch.
docs/feature-tests.md uses document.modelContext.getTools and executeTool with a discovered RegisteredTool, and states external action confirmation is required in Ask and Act modes.

verdict_a_intended_behavior_and_runtime_.verdict: SOURCE ROUTING CONTRACT ACCEPTED; NATIVE RUNTIME UNVERIFIED

evidence.assessment: The receiver rejects absent or already-closed origin tabs and passes the sender tab id. Dispatch keeps it on the ToolContext, where assigned-tab helpers resolve that tab rather than the current focus; a closed assigned tab resolves to null rather than falling back.

evidence.finding: Closed-origin failure is explicit at dispatch entry.
evidence.assessment: The dispatcher returns 'webmcp: origin tab unavailable' when the page tab closes before dispatch. The test evidence described in the builder report exercises a focus change and closure, but was not rerun in this review.

evidence.finding: Report records causal routing failures and successful final checks.
evidence.assessment: The report names separate bootstrap and dispatch causal REDs and records final test/typecheck commands as successful. I inspected the report and referenced source, without independently executing those commands.

verdict_a_intended_behavior_and_runtime_.runtime_limit: No supported Chrome build, enabled document.modelContext object, native discovery, or execution was observed. Chrome 149+ acceptance and exact extension-artifact provenance remain pending.

verdict_b_quality_and_doctrine.verdict: QUALITY ACCEPTED FOR THIS SOURCE REPAIR; NATIVE ACCEPTANCE REMAINS OPEN

evidence.finding: The fix is applied at the actual page-message ingress and retains the existing shared dispatcher gates.
evidence.assessment: Origin validation precedes dispatch. Existing external-call tier restrictions, admin-only checks, and mandatory action confirmation remain in handleWebmcpCall; assigned-tab transport does not grant new permissions.

evidence.finding: The repair report identifies the sibling callers of handleWebmcpCall.
evidence.assessment: Frontend and desktop callers do not carry a page sender tab, and the new optional field leaves their existing behavior intact.

evidence.finding: Feature procedures no longer describe callTool or promise external action execution without confirmation in Act mode.
evidence.assessment: The relevant procedures now use getTools/executeTool and describe confirmation in both modes, plus a real tab-switch and closed-tab acceptance scenario.

limitations: The test and typecheck evidence was read from committed output/report files, not rerun by this reviewer.
No live tab-switch or native WebMCP run was performed; the source-only review cannot close that acceptance requirement.
